label: National pension lump-sum refund: countries whose nationals may claim
appliesTo: Foreign nationals leaving Korea permanently who contributed to the national pension
why: Nationality decides this and the list is not intuitive — large countries with many workers in Korea are absent from it. The list is republished as agreements are concluded, so an old blog's country table is one of the more damaging things a departing worker can rely on.

history.source: National Pension Act, art. 126, and the social security agreements and reciprocity framework
history.note: 24 countries qualify through a social security agreement providing for the refund — the United States, Canada, Germany, Australia, France, India, Türkiye and the Philippines among them — and 26 through reciprocity, including Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Kazakhstan. China is not on the current list, so Chinese nationality alone does not establish entitlement. Minimum contribution conditions differ by country. Separately, periods contributed on E-8, E-9 or H-2 status qualify regardless of nationality. The basis for a foreign national's entitlement is art. 126 read with the social security agreements and reciprocity framework, not art. 102 — a citation that appears in many departure checklists and points at the wrong rule. Three routes exist: the home country recognising a corresponding benefit for Koreans, an agreement covering lump-sum refunds, or a qualifying residence status. Establish nationality and status against those routes before assuming any refund is payable.
